name: China Masters
stakes: This Super 750 event offers India a crucial opportunity to build on recent successes and rebound from setbacks, setting the tone for the latter half of the season.
summary:
India arrives at the China Masters, a Super 750 event, fresh off a mixed bag of performances at the recent BWF World Championships. The undeniable highlight was the historic bronze medal secured by the women's doubles pair of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand. Their "giant-killing spree" captivated fans, culminating in a hard-fought semi-final loss to the top seeds, but firmly establishing them as a formidable force on the circuit. They'll be looking to carry that momentum forward.

In men's doubles, the formidable duo of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty reached the quarterfinals before bowing out to a Chinese pair, reportedly battling fitness concerns. Their performance here will be closely watched to see if they've fully recovered and can reassert their dominance. PV Sindhu and Lakshya Sen, both aiming to rebound from earlier exits at the Worlds, will be eager to make a deeper run in Shenzhen. Veteran HS Prannoy and the rising mixed doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto also seek strong showings to climb the rankings.
